figure: Figure 11.3, red aggregate-KV caveat spanning panels A and B
issue: The single caveat spans both panels, but the aggregate check has sharply opposite consequences for the two cases, and the figure never says which case the aggregate actually breaks: on-node decode-side ingress is 4 × 450 = 1.8 TB/s vs 1.4 TB/s payload (feasible when spread, ~78–80% link utilization), while the cross-host path is 40 GB/s vs 1.4 TB/s (infeasible by ~35×). Every clause of the caveat is literally true, but the figure's entire purpose is to contrast A and B, and the caveat flattens that contrast.
evidence: Caveat text: '35 GB/request × 40 req/s = 1.4 TB/s of payload. Per-request times assume an unshared per-GPU link; 1.4 TB/s exceeds any single link above.' Arithmetic verified: 35 × 40 = 1400 GB/s ✓; 35/450 = 0.078 ≈ 0.08 s ✓; 35/40 = 0.875 ≈ 0.9 s ✓. Per-case check: A — 40 rps over 4 GPU pairs = 10 rps/pair × 0.08 s = 0.8 s/s ≈ 80% of one 450 GB/s link (feasible, tight, assumes even spread and TP-sharded KV); B — 40 rps × 0.9 s = 36 link-seconds/s needed vs 1 available ≈ 36× overcommit (infeasible). Note 11.3-1 (PDF 210 / printed 190) likewise stops at 'against the shared fabric' without the per-case aggregate arithmetic, so the reader gets no worked contrast anywhere.
root_cause: One caveat written for two regimes whose aggregate feasibility differs by ~45×; per-case aggregate never derived.
correction: Extend the caveat (or Note 11.3-1) with the per-case aggregate: 'A: 4 decode GPUs × 450 GB/s = 1.8 TB/s ingress can absorb 1.4 TB/s when spread (~80% per-link at 40 rps — feasible but tight); B: 40 GB/s NIC cannot (≈35× over) — so the transfer link, not topology alone, decides whether P/D disaggregation pays,' which also matches the chapter's own 'evaluate against measured phase conflict, not topology alone' guidance.
acceptance_test: The figure or Note 11.3-1 states the aggregate feasibility separately for case A and case B with the arithmetic (capacity vs 1.4 TB/s), and a reader cannot conclude that the on-node case fails at the canonical 40 rps peak.

issue: Panel A shows four prefill GPUs and four decode GPUs but a single KV arrow labeled '450 GB/s per GPU per direction'; the caveat compares aggregate 1.4 TB/s to 'any single link above' without noting the four-link aggregate (4 × 450 GB/s = 1.8 TB/s). A reader could infer the NVLink case cannot sustain the aggregate.
evidence: Panel A: '8× H100 host' with 4 orange prefill GPUs and 4 blue decode GPUs; one red KV arrow labeled '450 GB/s per GPU per direction'. Caveat: '35 GB/request × 40 req/s = 1.4 TB/s of payload' and '1.4 TB/s exceeds any single link above.' The panel's four NVLink links aggregate to ~1.8 TB/s, which exceeds 1.4 TB/s.
acceptance_test: Label the arrow with the aggregate capacity (e.g., '4 × 450 GB/s = 1.8 TB/s aggregate') or draw multiple links; clarify in the caveat that 1.4 TB/s exceeds one link but not necessarily the four-link aggregate. Verify the figure does not imply the NVLink case is infeasible at the stated load.

figure: FIGURE 11.3, panel A (Within one NVLink domain)
issue: The printed per-request on-node transfer time (0.08 s) is inconsistent with the figure's own 4-GPU prefill / 4-GPU decode grids and the 'per GPU' rate label. The top line reads '~35 GB ≈ 0.08 s' and the link is labeled '450 GB/s per GPU per direction', but 0.08 s = 35/450 treats the full 35 GB as traversing a single 450 GB/s link. With 4 prefill GPUs and 4 decode GPUs (TP sharding, which is mandatory for the canonical 70B since 140 GB > 80 GB per GPU), the 35 GB KV is split 4 ways and the 4 GPU-pair links run in parallel, so the per-request transfer latency is 35/(4·450) = 8.75/450 ≈ 0.02 s, i.e. 4× smaller than printed. Note 11.3-1 (p.190) repeats the single-link arithmetic: 'at NVLink's 450 GB/s per direction (§9.2) that transfer is 35 ÷ 450 ≈ 0.08 s'.
evidence: Panel A shows a 2×2 orange grid under 'PREFILL / 4 GPUs' and a 2×2 blue grid under 'DECODE / 4 GPUs'; link label '450 GB/s per GPU per direction'; header line '~35 GB ≈ 0.08 s (on-node, unidirectional)'. 35/450 = 0.0778 s (printed), but 35/(4·450) = 0.0194 s (implied by the 4 parallel GPU-pair links). The DP=4 reading that would justify 35 GB per link is infeasible for 70B (140 GB weights cannot replicate onto 80 GB GPUs).
acceptance_test: The printed on-node per-request time must equal 35 GB divided by the aggregate prefill→decode bandwidth implied by the depicted GPU count and per-GPU rate (≈0.02 s for 4 GPU pairs), OR the figure/note must explicitly state that 0.08 s is a single-unsharded-link conservative bound. The 'per GPU' label, the 4+4 GPU grids, and the 0.08 s figure must be mutually consistent; the same fix must be applied to Note 11.3-1 on p.190.

figure: FIGURE 11.3 (panel A, Within one NVLink domain)
issue: Panel A's header time and the drawn topology encode different transfer models. The header states the time for the WHOLE ~35 GB request KV over a single 450 GB/s link (35 / 450 = 0.078 s ~ 0.08 s), and the caption says the state 'crosses the joining link' (singular). But the panel draws 4 prefill GPUs and 4 decode GPUs with the KV arrow labeled '450 GB/s per GPU'. Under TP=4 the KV is sharded four ways, so each GPU ships ~8.75 GB over its own 450 GB/s link and the transfer completes in ~0.02 s. The figure therefore simultaneously implies a per-GPU link and a whole-state-over-one-link time, and the reader cannot tell which model the 0.08 s belongs to.
evidence: Rendered panel A: 'PREFILL / 4 GPUs' and 'DECODE / 4 GPUs' boxes, a single 'KV' arrow between them annotated '450 GB/s per GPU', header '~35 GB / 450 GB/s = 0.08 s (on-node, unidirectional)'. Page 190 note: '35 / 450 = 0.08 s'. Sharded alternative: 35/4 = 8.75 GB per GPU; 8.75/450 = 0.019 s.
acceptance_test: Panel A must pick one model and make it self-consistent: either (a) print the whole-state-over-one-link assumption explicitly ('whole 35 GB over one 450 GB/s link') and draw a single link, or (b) show the 4-way shard (per-GPU payload ~8.75 GB) and the resulting ~0.02 s. The printed time must be reproducible from the printed payload, link rate, and drawn topology, and the caption's 'crosses the joining link' must match the chosen model.

figure: FIGURE 11.3 (caption, token count vs KV size)
issue: The caption pairs a token count with a KV size that do not reconcile at the book's canonical KV rate. As rendered, the caption says 'the canonical 9.8K-token request carries ~24.1 GB'. At the canonical 2.62 MB/token (FP16, full-MHA 70B reference), 24.1 GB corresponds to 24,100/2.62 = 9,198 tokens, i.e. the canonical 9,200-token request (1,200 + 8,000), not 9.8K; a 9.8K-token request would carry 9,800 x 2.62 MB = 25.7 GB. One of the two numbers is wrong wherever this pair appears.
evidence: Rendered caption: 'the canonical 9.8K-token request carries ~24.1 GB'. Canonical KV rate 2.62 MB/token (house canonical, also used on PDF 210 / printed 190: '13.3K = 35 GB / 2.62 MB'). 35 GB / 2.62 MB = 13,359 tokens ~ 13.3K (consistent); 24.1 GB / 2.62 MB = 9,198 tokens ~ 9.2K (not 9.8K).
acceptance_test: Every place the canonical request's KV size is printed, the token count printed beside it must satisfy tokens x 2.62 MB/token = the stated KV size: 24.1 GB requires '9.2K-token' (9,200 = 1,200 + 8,000). If '9.8K' is printed, change it to '9.2K' or restate the KV size as 25.7 GB. Check the same pair in the Fig 11.3 caption and in Note 11.3-1 on PDF 210 / printed 190.

figure: Table 12-3 — Full-load feasibility matrix (conditional; not a deployment recommendation)
issue: Transposed divisor and quotient in the (a) cell of the 'Prefill hosts, peak 368K tok/s' row: '~19 (368K ÷ 18.6K ≈ 19.8) before headroom'. The per-host prefill rate for the 70B candidates is ~19,800 tok/s (stated in the prose directly above the table), so the correct working is 368K ÷ 19.8K ≈ 18.6 → ~19 hosts. As printed, the cell divides by the answer and reports the rate as the result; the two numbers inside the cell therefore contradict the '~19' host count printed beside them, and a reader recomputing from the prose rate lands on 18.6, not 19.8. The (c) cell in the same row uses the correct divisor-then-result order ('368,000 ÷ 24,725 ≈ 14.88'), which the (a) cell breaks.
evidence: printed 211 prose: 'Host counts are an illustrative capacity screen from the fixed per-host prefill profile: ~19,800 tok/s for the 70B candidates; ~24,700 tok/s for the 7B on the single H100 its layout declares — ~989 TFLOPS/s × 35% MFU ÷ 14 GFLOP/token'. Recomputation: 368,000 ÷ 19,800 = 18.59 → ~19 hosts; 92,000 ÷ 19,800 = 4.65 → ~5 hosts (matches the (a) avg cell '~5' and the (b) cells 'prefill pool ~5' / 'prefill pool ~19'). Printed (a) peak cell: '~19 (368K ÷ 18.6K ≈ 19.8) before headroom'.
acceptance_test: The cell reads '~19 (368K ÷ 19.8K ≈ 18.6) before headroom', and a reader recomputing 368,000 ÷ 19,800 from the prose rate reproduces the printed host count for (a), (b), and (c) without encountering a number that contradicts the cell's own host count.
